title: Ledger Live account data
whyItMatters: app.json lists every crypto account, its addresses and balance history. The keys stay on the hardware device, but the file shows what the person owns and how much.
source: Ledger Support, how to access the Ledger Wallet (formerly Ledger Live) user data file: app.json sits in the app's user data folder: https://support.ledger.com/article/8490479490333-zd
notes: Ledger Support documents the Linux user data folder as ~/.config/Ledger Live, and the folder keeps the Ledger Live name after the app was renamed Ledger Wallet. app.json holds accounts, settings and caches, never keys. Ledger publishes no Flatpak or Snap package, so this path covers the .deb and AppImage installs.

cleanup.exportFirst: Note the accounts shown in Ledger Wallet and keep the recovery phrase of the hardware wallet safe: only the account list lives on this computer.
steps: Confirm you have the recovery phrase or backup for this wallet.
Uninstall Ledger Wallet from the App Center if you are removing the app itself.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Deletes the account list, balance history and settings on this computer. The keys and funds stay on the hardware wallet.
cleanup.source: Ledger Support, Ledger Live user data file: https://support.ledger.com/article/8490479490333-zd
